title: Largest Reachable Meeting Value
statement:
You get two integers num and t. Pick any integer x. In one move you change x by +1 or −1 and at the same time change num by +1 or −1; the two directions are chosen independently.

Call x reachable if, after at most t moves, x and num are equal. Return the largest reachable x.

examples.why: Start with x = 7. Lower x to 6 and raise num to 6 in the same move: they meet.
Each move closes the gap by 2, so three moves close a gap of 6. Answering num + t = 5 forgets that num moves too.

hints: In one move, by how much can the gap between x and num shrink at most?
Move x toward num and num toward x at the same time: the gap shrinks by 2 per move.
After t moves you can close any gap up to 2t, so the largest x is num + 2t.

explain.intuition:
Only the gap x − num matters. Each move changes both numbers by 1. If they step toward each other, the gap shrinks by 2; any other choice shrinks it by 0 or grows it. So with t moves the largest gap you can close is 2t, and the largest x is num + 2t.

"At most t moves" is not needed for this answer, but it matters for odd gaps: a gap of 1 can never close, because the gap's parity never changes. The maximum avoids that by using an even gap.
steps: Notice each move changes the gap by −2, 0 or +2.
The best is −2 every move, so t moves close a gap of 2t.
pitfalls: Returning num + t, as if only x moved.
Thinking the gap can shrink by more than 2 per move.

solutions.title: Simulate from the top
solutions.idea: Try x from high to low, simulating the best moves (both step toward each other) and return the first x that meets num within t moves.

solutions.title: Close the gap by two per move
solutions.idea: Each move shrinks the gap by at most 2, so the answer is num + 2t.

followups: Return how many integers x are reachable.
Each move may change x by up to a and num by up to b. What is the largest reachable x now?
